title: Action Verification through Conjecture and Refutation for Language Model Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.02950v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Language model agents increasingly act on users' behalf by manipulating external environments through tools, often from high-level instructions that leave critical task- and environment-specific context unstated. To prevent resulting misaligned actions, recent work verifies proposed actions before execution, largely by establishing whether the conditions supporting them hold. We argue that this confirmation-oriented view leaves a fundamental blind spot: a wrong action often passes every check that asks whether it is right. This motivates a different question for verification: rather than asking what evidence supports an action, can the agent find evidence that refutes it? We pursue this direction with BlackSwan, a refutation-oriented, expect-suspect-test procedure that predicts the intended effect of each state-mutating action, formulates specific and empirically testable hypotheses for how it could be wrong, and tests them using exist

translated_title: 面向语言模型智能体的基于猜想与反驳的动作验证
translated_abstract: 语言模型智能体越来越多地通过工具操控外部环境来代表用户执行任务，而这些任务通常源自高级指令，其中关键的任务特定和环境特定上下文往往未被明确说明。为了防止由此产生的不当行为，近期的工作会在执行前对拟议动作进行验证，主要是通过确认支持该动作的条件是否成立。我们认为这种以确认为导向的观点存在一个根本性盲区：一个错误的动作往往能够通过所有询问“它是否正确”的检查。这促使我们对验证提出一个不同的问题：与其询问什么证据支持一个动作，智能体能否找到反驳它的证据？我们沿这一方向提出了BlackSwan，这是一种以反驳为导向的“预期-怀疑-检验”流程，它预测每个改变状态的动作的预期效果，为该动作可能出错的方式制定具体的、可实证检验的假设，并进行检验……
tldr: 该论文提出BlackSwan，一种受“猜想与反驳”思想启发的动作验证方法，通过预测动作的预期效果并主动构造、检验可能推翻动作正确性的具体假设，从而捕捉传统确认式验证无法发现的不当智能体行为。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes BlackSwan, a refutation-oriented verification procedure for language model agents that predicts intended action effects and actively formulates and tests falsifiable hypotheses about how an action could be wrong, catching misaligned actions that confirmation-based checks miss.
